claims.statement: EMA's qualification pathway is evidence-based and explicitly covers novel biomarkers and digital methodologies, while EHDS will phase in governed reuse of health data. A founder can start with an ethically consented, recontactable Polish cohort and reusable reference-test protocol, but proprietary reuse rights and regulatory acceptability require confirmation.

The paid event is a sponsor choosing a wearable-derived endpoint or digital measure for a trial and needing evidence that the technology is fit for purpose. FDA guidance makes verification, validation, participant suitability, and data integrity concrete requirements; the cost of a failed endpoint decision is sponsor-specific.

The payer hypothesis is a biotech sponsor, wearable maker, or specialist CRO using clinical-development or validation budget before protocol lock. Regulators describe the required evidence pathway, but a small Warsaw-based study operator has not demonstrated procurement access or price.

contrary_evidence: Large CROs, academic sites, and wearable manufacturers already run validation studies and hold sponsor relationships.
EHDS may improve broad access to governed health data, reducing the scarcity value of a small proprietary cohort while imposing strict controls.

economics.acquisition_route: Design one narrow fatigue or cognitive-function validation protocol with an ethics and clinical partner, pre-sell it to a wearable company, and recruit 30-100 participants only after the sponsor funds study operations.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Reusable endpoint protocols, normative datasets, and a recontactable cohort can shift revenue from one-off studies toward benchmark licensing and multi-sponsor trials; reaching the founder objective requires repeat sponsor demand and defensible consented reuse.
economics.founder_time: Roughly 15-20 hours per week during study setup and analysis, with participant operations, medical oversight, and ethics handled by contracted partners.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Analysis and protocol reuse are high-margin; participant compensation, reference tests, ethics, devices, and clinical partner fees are direct study costs.
economics.payback: Do not recruit before a sponsor milestone covers variable costs; recover protocol-development cost within the first two studies.
economics.pricing: Fixed protocol and study fee with participant costs passed through, followed by annual benchmark or reference-data licenses where consent permits.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Sponsors repeat by population and endpoint; recontactable participants and harmonized methods reduce subsequent study time.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented longitudinal neurocognitive reference data, participant recontact rights, and regulator-aware reusable validation protocols
fingerprint.customer: Wearable manufacturers, digital-health developers, biotech trial sponsors, and specialist CROs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner referrals from CROs and academic investigators plus direct outreach at protocol-design stage
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Sponsor-funded remote validation studies plus licensing of consented benchmark datasets and protocols
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Clinical-development team pays before protocol lock when a digital measure needs fit-for-purpose evidence
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A sponsor wants continuous wearable data but lacks population-specific evidence linking it to a credible reference measure

founder_fit: The founder combines neuroscience, biosignal experience, statistics, and AI-enabled study analysis.
A Poland-based remote cohort can be operated without a camera-led personal brand.
Sponsor prepayment can cap capital exposure and keep the work compatible with part-time execution.
risks: Human-subject research, GDPR, medical-device, and clinical-trial rules may make the wedge slower and more expensive than assumed.
Consent language may not permit the desired cross-sponsor data reuse.
A small cohort may not satisfy endpoint validation or qualification requirements.

structure.commercial_archetype: Contract research wedge compounding into a consented benchmark-data asset
structure.control_point: Reusable protocol plus participant consent, reference-linked data, and recontact rights
structure.critical_dependency: Ethically and legally reusable data that sponsors regard as fit-for-purpose evidence

thesis: Backcast from trials where continuous digital endpoints are routine: own the expensive bridge between raw wearable signals and credible reference outcomes now, using sponsor-funded micro-studies to build a reusable European neurocognitive benchmark asset.
title: Wearable Endpoint Foundry
uncertainties: Which single endpoint has urgent sponsor demand and an affordable reference standard is unresolved.
Sponsor procurement cycles and acceptable Polish site credentials are unknown.
It is unproven that benchmark licensing can be separated from custom study work.
